reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
I heard that it was a tuna restaurant launched by Kim Soo-sa, a powerhouse of Korean Japanese food, so I was expecting a “good restaurant~”, but in the end, it was not an authentic tuna restaurant, but rather a tuna version of Kim Soo-sa’s ‘rich course’.
The 70,000 won course (+ 10,000 won corkage) is surprisingly cost-effective.

However, the service details are disappointing.
The friendly aunts greet us warmly, but their explanations of what kind of fish it is and what sauce to dip it in are confusing.
Considering the value of the name, this gap in guidance is a pretty big point of deduction.

The flow of the course is centered around ‘the taste of filling your stomach’.
The starter black sesame porridge was seasoned well, but the rice grains were a bit clumpy, and on the other hand, the corn cheese was the early winner of the day - the cheese was properly melted, not a sloppy mayo, so I was tempted to refill it.
The tuna skewers start well with wasabi and seaweed toppings, and the shiso rice bowl that follows fills the stomach.

The highlight was the tuna rib performance.
Take the whole rib bone, scrape it out with a spoon, and serve half raw and the other half with yukhoe seasoning and yolk as ‘tuna yukhoe.’
Honestly, the seasoned version is better than the raw tuna - the sweetness of the tuna, the richness of the soy sauce, and the viscosity of the yolk are just right.

Now for the main sashimi plate.
There are approximately 6 pieces per person, but the cuts are large, so the experience is plentiful.
Red meat (akami) has a distinct iron flavor, making it the character of the day (there are likes and dislikes).
The belly fat line was in good condition, and the key was to eat quickly before the water started flowing.

It's a bit disappointing that the horse mackerel has a gentle tone like white meat rather than the bright oil of 'blue back'.
The tuna sushi on the side is surprisingly refreshing when paired with shiso rice.
The stewed tuna ribs were light and clean, and the ginkgo nuts on the side had a pleasant kick—I just wish the temperature was a little warmer.

The second half is full of “stomach filling parts.”
The fried shrimp was textbook, but the fish meat burger was lacking in bread and was off balance.
However, the bibim noodles are the turning point of the day - they are moderately spicy and will rejuvenate your taste buds.
The udon was bland, and the spicy stew was spicy.
The dessert ice cream has a pretty assortment, but the taste is average.

To sum it up, it is not a “course that is suspenseful with just tuna.”
Instead, Kim Soo-sa's strengths—plenty of food, things to see, and filling—were put on the theme of tuna.
Personally, I found the course structure, which allows red wine, to be interesting (corkage fee of 10,000 won), but it may be a bit disappointing if you say, ‘I will only eat elaborate tuna.’
On the other hand, if you are looking for a tuna course that several people can enjoy while eating in a variety of ways, and if the concept is “Let’s eat our fill today,” there is a high probability that you will be satisfied.

small tip
- Belly fat first: Enjoy it quickly before the water melts away.
- Be proactive in requesting explanations: Be sure to ask about the fish/sauce pairing.
- Wine pairing: Medium red (Pino/light Rhone) also works surprisingly well.
- Plenty of quantity: Speed ​​control of carbohydrates in the second half.

As for the food, the appetizer of Korean beef wrapped in crispy seaweed was unique, had a good texture, and was very delicious. The soft, bubbling button mushroom soup was really delicious, and the pork bacon was also delicious (the bacon was pork belly, of course). The grilled bread was also crispy and delicious. The main ribs are very tender ribs, and they are sliced ​​well so you can eat them to your fill. reviews.text:
In Apgujeong, Seoul, there is a very special pork restaurant called ‘Musik’.

People who hear this name for the first time may feel a little unfamiliar.

In fact, the 'radish' in 'Musik' means radish, but here it has more meaning than just an ingredient. This is the cooking philosophy of ignorance.

Many Korean barbecue restaurants tend to focus solely on the meat itself.

However, in radish, dishes are designed around radishes.

Radish is an essential ingredient on Korean tables. You can add it to soup or kimchi, or enjoy it as a crunchy and sweet side dish. The combination of fatty pork and crunchy, sweet radish creates a more balanced and delicious flavor.

It is this simple yet often overlooked combination that I am talking about in Ignorance. The key is to preserve the natural taste of the ingredients rather than complicated recipes.

The pork used here is airlifted from Goheung, Jeollanam-do, South Korea. Thanks to a stable breeding and supply system, the quality of meat is consistently high.

The variety of radish dishes on the table makes the entire meal more refreshing and comforting.

The name “ignorant” has another meaning. It means simplicity, unadornment, and lack of decoration. There is no excessive decoration here, just carefully prepared food.

Pork is, of course, an important ingredient in musik.

But it's that refreshing bite of radish that truly impresses.

One bite of meat, one bite of radish. Simple but perfect balance.

reviews.text: Sponsored // Tatsu Robatasho is an izakaya where you can truly feel the sensibility of robatayaki on Garosu-gil. Because it is centered around Tachi Seok, it has a live feel as it is grilled right on the charcoal fire, and thanks to the fire scent that spreads throughout the space, you will be intoxicated with the atmosphere as soon as you enter. The charcoal grilled chicken platter is full of firey flavor on the outside and moist on the inside, providing a good balance of textures, and the lily clam nabe has a refreshing broth that cleanses the palate. It is a place with valet parking and accessibility, so I recommend it for a drink on Garosu-gil.

reviews.text: While looking for an izakaya with a quiet atmosphere near Shinsa Station, I visited Tatsu Robatasho. Located inside an alley, it is not crowded, and the wood-toned interior and calm lighting create a comfortable atmosphere. The main focus was robata cuisine using charcoal fire, and the seasonal grilled fish was light but still had a fiery taste, so we were highly satisfied. Tongyeong oyster charcoal-grilled ceviche was enjoyed without feeling greasy with its refreshing sauce, and the grilled eggplant added as a separate item was also impressive with its chewy texture and savory flavor. This is a recommended shrine izakaya that is perfect for dates or small drinking parties.

reviews.author: gap kku

The moment I sat at the bar table and watched the chef grilling skewers over charcoal, I felt like I was watching a performance rather than just the act of eating. The high ceiling and open space make you feel comfortable, and the softly lit interior creates a natural date atmosphere. The course, which starts with a highball and continues with hormone skewers and flounder sushi, is a perfect combination of alcohol and snacks, and the menu that pays special attention to visuals is also recommended as a ‘restaurant that is good for taking pictures.’ It's great for conversation and enjoyment in a lively atmosphere, and it's also a great date spot near Garosu-gil and Sinsa Station. You can experience a special day by visiting with friends or lovers during a leisurely evening and enjoying home-cooked dishes, fragrant charcoal scent, fresh seafood, and alcohol. Tatsurobatasho is a place I highly recommend to those who want to create a memorable experience that satisfies all five senses, rather than just a meal to fill the stomach.

reviews.author: Hye sung Kim
reviews.text: I went to Sinsa Station Izakaya where all the snacks were delicious. There was a discount event on wine and sake. I really recommend the flatfish ceviche. The skewers come out really well too. It has a nice atmosphere and is delicious, so I recommend it as a gentleman’s bar.^^

reviews.author: Summer
reviews.text:
I came to the shrine on Monday evening. We are from Canada. While I was walking, I saw this restaurant and went in. Beautiful interior, nice atmosphere, and friendly staff. The food is super delicious too!
I ordered shrimp ceviche and tuna tataki.

I recommend this place~~

On a monday night we decided to come to Shinsa and wander around. we found this place randomly, and decided to have a try.
it seems a lot of famous people came by. we ordered the shrimp ceviche and the tuna tataki, they are delicious!! better than expected!

They have good ambiance, great music, the decor is beautiful with separate curtains, staff is friendly, totally recommend this place.

reviews.author: freetempo Yamada
reviews.text:
Third visit.
This is Azakaya located on Garosu-gil.
Every time I went, I ordered and ate different menu items, but they all tasted great and the food came out beautifully presented on a plate.
Moderately crowded atmosphere
Because it was in a room format, there was no problem in having a quiet conversation even if we went during busy times. I really hate talking with my voice raised. Like other bars in Garosu-gil, the prices are a bit high.
The staff are all friendly and valet parking is available.
I think I'll visit again if I have an appointment nearby.

reviews.author: Dosuni VLOG
reviews.text: Since it's an izakaya, I didn't know they specialize in food, but the ingredients are fresh and the food quality is very good. The futomaki is delicious with shrimp tempura, salmon, and tuna. The shrimp tempura clothing is crispy and the shrimp are delicious. Be sure to add raw noodles to Nagasaki Jjamppong!

First review on Google!!
Reservation visit for Dusara set menu for 2 people


Tataki Uni Amaebi Sashimi in the Clouds

reviews.author: Ji Wook Jang
reviews.text:
Room type izakaya
Friendly service and every meal was delicious. Reservations were fully booked after 7pm on Friday, so we only used the 2-hour visit at 5pm.
Reservations are recommended.

reviews.author: manul garlic
reviews.text: Godpouo, located in Sinsa-dong, is a Japanese izakaya restaurant. There are so many menus that even people who can't eat raw fish can enjoy a drink here. The advantage of this place is that it has rooms. It is a room-type carriage made up of small rooms, but it boasts quick service, perhaps due to its simple interior and many staff. The taste of the snacks is above average, so if you want to have a quiet drink with friends in Sinsa-dong, I recommend looking for it.

reviews.author: Ya Hong
reviews.text:
“Kappo Uo” competes in Kappo cuisine with great taste at a reasonable price.

The first dish is a special assorted plate. The contents are plentiful, including bluefin tuna, sea urchin, sweet shrimp, and scallops, but the taste and quantity exceed expectations.

Hotate fry. The combination of the soft flesh of the fried scallops and the crispy batter is good, and the sauce is also excellent.

Marbled Tantan Nabe. Generous portion and spicy yet sweet taste of cabbage. And the combination of raw udon noodles was quite good.

Kaisentomatoni. I like the sour tomato sauce and the chewy texture of the cuttlefish and shrimp.

The fried shrimp served was also good.

reviews.author: D.W.C Love
reviews.text: All the tables are in rooms, and it's not easy to get a seat because it's so popular, but the facilities are really neat and tidy. Although the price is a bit high, I would like to say that the taste and freshness are truly the best. There are a lot of snacks and drinks, and the staff is friendly, so it's a great place to have a quiet drink in your room.

reviews.author: Should I dream (Should I dream)
reviews.text:
I knew it was a room, but I expected a slightly casual atmosphere...
It was the first twist in a fairly luxurious atmosphere.
In fact, there are expected prices and portion sizes at a typical Japanese restaurant.
So today, I decided not to eat too much and ordered 3 dishes.
The unexpected amount was the second twist.

Quality of ingredients, quantity and taste of food
Everything was perfect.🫡

And the whole time I was using it, I felt like it was quieter than I expected.
I thought it would be noisy, but I enjoyed it privately.

I am 100% willing to revisit.

reviews.author: yuntae Kim
reviews.text:
I went to Shinsaman Eel with the staff and ordered a special lunch set + eel rice bowl for two.

The eel, which is grilled directly on charcoal, has a unique shine, is crispy on the outside and really moist on the inside.

There is no fishy smell at all and the seasoning is not too much, so it's perfect to eat with rice.

The two-person set was well-organized, so I was satisfied with the grilled food, side dishes, and side dishes, and the eel rice bowl special had a generous amount of eel, so it was hearty.

Even during lunch time, the place is quick and the staff is friendly, making it a recommended place for a company dinner or team lunch. Next time, I want to come back with my family.

Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Mongbi
reviews.text:
I went to Sinsaman Eel, a restaurant with eel rice bowls at Sinsa Station!

I had the special eel rice bowl with a large eel including its tail, and it was really delicious. It was the best food that went well with various sauces and side dishes without any fuss. I highly recommend it for dates, gatherings, or invitations around people.

reviews.author: Kyeong-eun Lee
reviews.text: I recommend Gangnam Room Restaurant, which is close to Sinsa Station and is great for a company dinner! A neat and delicious grilled eel! The menu is so good and delicious that I am amazed every time I eat it. I recommend it as a place for year-end gatherings!

reviews.author: Eunjeong Kim
reviews.text: Sinsaman Eel, a restaurant near Sinsa Station famous for its eel rice bowl!! The seasoning is so delicious that you will end up eating it again and again. If you are on a date on Garosu-gil, be sure to visit as it is a room restaurant. You can also get eel soup as a service during the day^^

reviews.author: Park Dasom
reviews.text:
Looking for a good restaurant at Sinsa Station with friends
A place I visited to take care of myself during the winter!
It was nice to be able to dine with just the group as there was a separate room space, and it seemed like many people visited Garosu-gil for dates.

The eel was plump and had a chewy texture, so 3 people visited and all 3 enjoyed it.
I highly recommend half and half sauce!
It can be a bit greasy and bite you, but I ate every last bit of the eel, and the side dishes were so good that I ate it all up!
Recognized as a good restaurant at Sinsa Station~

It takes 40 minutes for food to come out after ordering.
Tables that arrived 20 minutes late were immediately served.
The taste was average, but I got really annoyed when it came out late.

reviews.author: Eric Ng
reviews.text: I came from Malaysia and visited this place and had no regrets. There are so many people, but the beef broth is really delicious! It's really filling when eaten with meat. Imagine eating and drinking warm broth in cold weather. It feels like I'm in heaven!

reviews.author: Tiffany Chan
reviews.text:
The atmosphere is really lively. It's the perfect place to hang out with friends, and the food is really delicious. All the meat is fresh and cooked very well.

In particular, I ate fresh sashimi and high-quality beef in the hot pot, and it was really delicious. It's the kind of place where you want to have a drink, forget all your worries and spend time comfortably.

reviews.author: David Tan
reviews.text: The combination of top quality beef and rich broth is truly delicious. If you go to Gangnam, be sure to try it.

reviews.author: Myungji Bae
reviews.text:
I went there through a friend's recommendation, and I was so satisfied that I returned with other friends.

The atmosphere is really nice (I felt like I was teleported somewhere in Europe in the bustling Garosu-gil alley..? haha)

The food is very delicious. The menu is diverse, and there are many different types of menus, from basic menus that anyone will like to unique menus, so it's fun to choose from. :) After writing this review, I want to go again.

Garosu-gil is recommended as a restaurant, meeting place, date place, and blind date place~!

reviews.author: Tony's TV (Tony's TV)
reviews.text:
It’s a unique space where steak and yakitori coexist. It was nice to be able to choose a menu according to each person's taste, and I was surprised that Bong Sushi was of the same quality as most sushi restaurants.
It's an izakaya specializing in charcoal grills with a New York atmosphere. I'm not sure where in New York it is, but the food was delicious haha.
Please note that if there is a wait, store operating hours are 2 hours and 30 minutes, and valet service is also available, so please inquire for more details.

reviews.author: Jiyoon Shin
reviews.text: Although it is an izakaya, it has a mix of Western styles, so it is great for foreigners to enjoy without too much pressure. Unlike other izakayas, the food is very diverse, the overall quality of the food is high, and the atmosphere is also good for a date. There is also group seating, so it is no problem to come with family. And most of all, the staff are very friendly and provide good service, and I enjoyed the comfortable atmosphere. I will have to go again 😍😍

reviews.author: Seungmin Ha
reviews.text: The atmosphere and lighting were really nice and the food was really delicious!! The owner was really kind and took care of the service from time to time, which was nice! I think I will visit often in the future~~

reviews.author: chan
reviews.text: It feels like they put a lot of thought into every detail of the menu! The atmosphere is really nice, and I happened to come in while visiting a gentleman, and I'm completely satisfied. 💛💛 Oh, there are a lot of people on blind dates. Haha. I think it's good for blind dates or wedding invitation gatherings! I'll go again next time✨

reviews.author: Lever Mint
reviews.text:
It was corkage free and I enjoyed it.
I only made a reservation for 2pm, but I saw that we had to wait for over 10 minutes?? I did it, but
In general, the food was good. There were 4 sauces, so you could eat it with the sauce that suited your taste. The taste of the mushrooms and meat wasn't bad. The store was basically pretty, and I was surprised by the large number of customers.
The downside is that since shabu-shabu and grilling are provided at the same time, it is impossible to control the heat separately, so it is a bit difficult to control the tempo of eating. In general, it tries to be friendly and kind, but perhaps because it is busy, it feels a bit unfriendly, but it is still not a bad place.

reviews.author: kinoi p
reviews.text:
The boss seems to have a very strong ego. It seems friendly, but it is very uncomfortable even after hearing the menu explanation. While teaching you how to eat it yourself, almost all the vegetables are added to the shabu shabu without the customer's consent. It needs to be slightly boiled before eating, but it's annoying to put so much in it and have to quickly scoop it out and eat it while it's still hot before the vegetables spread. Moreover, when I inquired about vegetable refills to eat more, I was told to refill them separately. Tsk tsk~~ Customers have their own tastes... but the food tastes good no matter where you go. However, the grill is unique so you can boil broth and grill brisket (so you can eat brisket wrapped in Vietnamese spring rolls), but it is very inconvenient. There is a speed to wrap and eat Vietnamese spring rolls, but the meat board needs to be continuously grilled, so it has to be heated, and the broth boils together for no reason, so you have to squeeze it and add additional broth.... Is it unmanageable? The boss, for some reason, eats the vegetables he put in all at once. It's a mess. In the end, the kalguksu or porridge broth that you eat at the last minute already has a strong salty taste, so even if you pour water instead of broth, you cannot feel the original soft porridge taste.
In short, this house made an effort to differentiate itself, but it makes many people uncomfortable.
The price is also reasonable. Was the owner's signature set menu 29,500 won? Anyway, if there is a reason to eat shabu-shabu at Garosu-gil, changing jobs is not a good idea.

reviews.author: sunni
reviews.text: The service is so good that you can enjoy a delicious meal even without looking at the menu! It tastes okay. You can get more vegetables from the self-service bar. The portion is large and just right!

reviews.author: Hyunjoong Kim
reviews.text:
Garosu-gil, Sinsa-dong
A restaurant with parking available near Sinsa Station.
Even valet parking...
Shabu-shabu, Vietnamese spring roll, brisket and kalguksu,
A place where you can enjoy fried rice all at once.
They even offer unlimited refills of Vietnamese spring rolls.
This is a place like this for steamed restaurants.
Friendly, delicious, and totally good~!

reviews.author: amy choi
reviews.text:
A set consisting of shabu-shabu, Vietnamese spring rolls, noodle soup, and porridge.
Shabu-shabu, Vietnamese spring rolls, and kalguksu are all delicious. I actually don't know what the porridge tastes like... If you order for two, two people can eat to their heart's content. Vegetables are also fresh. The staff is also friendly. I plan to come again next time to eat Vietnamese spring rolls. Valet parking available (3,000 won?)

reviews.author: Bologna
reviews.text:
Taste: Karaimen is not as spicy as expected and the meat broth is rich and oily.  I think soft boiled eggs should definitely be added. Gyoza has a plain taste. Evidong is also so so.
Store: Convenient as you can order using the device at your seat and pay directly by credit card.

reviews.author: D.W.C Love
reviews.text: It's been a while since I moved here from another location on Garosu-gil, but the store is larger than before, so it feels much more open and it's nice to have a place where I can eat alone. As expected from a famous Japanese ramen restaurant, the soup tastes deep and rich, and the noodles are cooked just right. The harmony between the noodles and the soup is excellent. The prices are reasonable, and you can only prepay by table order.

reviews.author: Angela “Anji” Jang
reviews.text:
You must always pay by yourself with a pad.
And ramen’s soft-boiled eggs aren’t the standard. Please keep in mind that you will need to add more eggs!
The broth is not thick, and Stamina Tonkotsu Ramen contains minced garlic and garlic chips, which help to cool down the body. It's also good for eating alone.

reviews.author: DJ KIM
reviews.text:
This is a Japanese ramen restaurant located in the alley next to Garosu-gil near Sinsa Station.
It is said to be a ramen restaurant that started in Japan in 1973 and opened in Seoul in 2008.
Unlike the somewhat improved tonkotsu ramen commonly found in Korea, it tastes like traditional Japanese broth... There may be some likes and dislikes about the salty yet deep and rich broth, but it's perfect for my taste.

#Saga Ramen #Garosu-gil Restaurant #Sinsa Station Restaurant #Japanese Ramen #Close to the taste of authentic tonkotsu ramen

reviews.author: elilolulolilela Al (Jk)
reviews.text:
Not bad ramen. Even 5 years ago, I would have thought it was absolutely delicious, but just like 🍔, there has been a lot of upward standardization, so it doesn't seem to be very impressive now. Still, I think this is a place in Sinsa-dong where you can get the best value for this taste at this price.

Still, the rich soup and thin noodles of the tonkotsu ramen were excellent, perhaps because it was made by a master. I also really liked the fact that the salinity can be adjusted. Unless you like it very salty, I would personally recommend the normal salt level, which is the default setting.

It would be a bit disappointing if the ramen had included a soft-boiled egg or seaweed, or if the chashu had been thicker or had been given three pieces.

reviews.author: Namho Kim (Chaos K)
reviews.text:
It was so delicious that I thought it was first tier among conveyor belt sushi franchises. The aged raw sushi and karaage were especially delicious!

The sauces, such as garlic and buldak, were spicy, so it was nice to eat them one at a time.

I plan to visit again!

reviews.text:
The best sushi from chain restaurants. There is a wait, but it's worth the wait.
The Sinsa branch is small, but the atmosphere is lively.
The taste is great for the price.  The Gangnam branch is large, so if several people are visiting, go to the Gangnam branch.

I often go to Godden Sushi at the Gangnam branch, so I went in thinking it would be similar since it was a chain restaurant.
The lunch set had less variety compared to Gangnam, and the taste was somewhat lacking. Maybe it was the seasoning, but it didn't taste like delicious sushi and was somewhat boring. Even though my mouth is bland, the taste is boring, so you can see that it's really bland. The store is small, and there are only 3 table seats. I was a little hungry, so I ordered takoyaki, but it was sour because there was a lot of ketchup on it, and there was too much flour dough than octopus inside, so I didn't like it.

reviews.author: D.W.C Love
reviews.text: It is truly top tier among franchise conveyor belt sushi restaurants. Since the store is small, there is always a wait, but if you go after lunch time, there will be little or no waiting, so it is better to aim for that time. The staff is really friendly and you can have a satisfactory meal.

reviews.author: Lee Dong-hyun (connector)
reviews.text:
If you're wondering where you can enjoy light conveyor belt sushi, it's easy to think of Godden Sushi.
Because it is good value for money and although the quality is not high, it is not bad either.
I tried eating medium and large belly fat separately, but I was disappointed.
Menus with well-balanced sauces are light and delicious to eat.
It is also satisfying to be able to make and drink warm green tea.

reviews.text:
Dishes you can't eat even in Japan

I ordered 4 dishes: Kaisendon, Uni Avocado Oil Pasta, Shimesaba Capellini, and Grilled Kani Miso.

First of all, the main ingredient in all menus was seafood, but none of them had a fishy smell.

The menu items that were particularly impressive were the capellini and uni pasta. The sesame sauce and thin capellini noodles went well together with the shimesaba, and the uni avocado had a good combination of the scent of uni and avocado with the thick linguine noodles.

The herring was better than any restaurant, so I ate herring sushi twice. I ate it with wine... The sushi and wine went so well together, and it was even better because they matched well.

reviews.author: Ryan Kim
reviews.text: It was a clean and neat meal. I have always enjoyed delicious food since I lived in Bundang. All of them are very delicious, without missing anything. The salty shari goes well with the oily netas, and when you finish it off with maki-ryu, the cucumbers leave your mouth feeling refreshed, making it a perfect meal.

reviews.author: Dongmin Lee

It was disappointing that there was no blue-backed fish, but it was a good meal.
It felt a little messy and it felt a bit awkward to hold the nigiri, but the composition was good so I could get over it. Ankimo is a bit too sweet and there are a lot of other things.
I didn't feel like putting it in. It feels a bit monotonous to finish all nigiri with green tangerine, but at the side counter, it costs 120,000 won, and I am satisfied.

reviews.text:
Visited on 23.02.06

Corkage available (50,000 won)

Although I live in Bundang, I have never been able to go there due to tight reservations, but thanks to a friend, I was able to get a chance to go.

Since Tsumami is the type of drink that calls for alcohol, I got drunk earlier than expected, so my friend took my share of the photos in the latter part of the picture ㅡㅡ;;;

I 100% intend to return, but they say they are leaving Bundang and moving to Shinsa ㅜㅜ....

reviews.author: WON KIM

Each dish has a sense of the season, and the colorful yet neat plating raises expectations even before you taste it.

The taste was also intuitive and distinct, so it seemed familiar and suited my taste. Personally, even in Japan, I like kaiseki, which is closer to Kappo than traditional kaiseki, and it reminded me of the dishes of Nagahori and Ichiyo Shimanouchi in Osaka.

I think not only the taste but also the composition and quantity were the best. This seems to be the best option when you want delicious Japanese food and Japanese sake.

reviews.author: ini KIM
reviews.text: I went for lunch on a weekday. There was valet, so I went right in without worrying about parking. I arrived 3 minutes before 12:00 and sat at the counter bar. At 12:00 sharp, I heard exciting music and a black curtain (?) went up. The moment the chefs appeared ㅋㅋㅋ̆̈ㅋ̆̎ㅋ̊̈ I really like this performance~ I was excited from the start!! There was only an omakase course for lunch, so I trusted it and ate it. It's beyond my expectations. It was a course that fully utilized the original taste of the ingredients. It was a meal of grilled geumtae and glutinous rice. The orinabe soup was amazing!! I want to go again~ I really liked the bright and young atmosphere, and the food was very good. May you prosper :D

reviews.author: thebitnaalMore Shine
reviews.text:
The atmosphere was nice, the staff were friendly, and the food was good.
Perhaps because it was a lunch menu, there was less variety than expected.
If you just want to eat seafood, this is the place to go, but if you want to enjoy seafood and other Japanese food as well, it's worth a visit at least once!

Even if I go back for dinner, I don't think I'll go back for lunch.

#Sinsa-dong #Yasai Makikuisinbo

“A disappointment hidden by the still deliciousness and casualness.”

One of my favorite izakayas, Kuishinbo Brothers, is a casual bar that specializes in rolled vegetable skewers. Since I already reviewed it in great detail in my first review, rather than a detailed review, I would like to talk about how I felt after visiting for the first time in a long time...

This visit feels different from when I sat at Dachi, perhaps because I sat at a table other than Dachi.
The advantages here are still the same
1.Sales of domestic soju
2. Delicious
3. Kindness
4. Not too expensive
5. Easy to make reservations

But I have some regrets...
1. The perfection of grilled skewers is lower than before.
Grilling skewers is not an easy skill even in Japan, so much so that it is called a craftsmanship, and rolling vegetables is even more so. It is a difficult technique in terms of temperature and time because the grilling temperature of the meat on the outside and the vegetables on the inside are different, but in these skewers, there is a lot of disharmony between the texture of the vegetables and the texture of the meat on the outside. In addition, the yakisoba and sukiyaki that I enjoyed so much in the past feel like I am eating the dish in one bite, but the perfection is not as good as before.
2. The pork in the pork shabu-shabu is frozen front leg meat, so the meat is dry and tasteless. You can't feel the softness and meaty flavor that is unique to pork shabu. It may not be a specialty restaurant, but honestly, the meat is terrible!
Fortunately, the dashi soup is delicious and suitable for spoon-feeding.

Nevertheless, the reason why I rate it as delicious is...
1. First of all, it’s delicious. Although it is a bit disappointing, the skewers are still powerful.
2. The ham cutlass was unexpectedly good, and the Neapolitan was salty for a bar Neapolitan, making it good as a side dish.
3. I ate too much, but the quality of the milk pudding they gave me was exceptional haha. It's a year-end night where I'm enjoying Kuishinbo, which is still at the top of my izakaya list.

PS: The skewer basket performance that was shown in the past is no longer there ㅠㅠ

**Built with my own money / Not sponsored / Not an acquaintance / Just one of the countless visitors who came with admiration**

Here is the ideal pub you have been longing for.
Food quality, attractive menu composition and excellent hospitality.
Here is a Japanese restaurant that is close to ‘perfect’ and has all three elements.

As the name of the business suggests, 'Warayaki', which means grilling on a straw fire, is the signature, but all menu items are at a level that would be worthy of serving as the main signature, and it feels like a dish that has been reborn by combining high-quality ingredients with advanced techniques.

The food seems simple and undifferentiated, so you may wonder why they talk so much about technique and go overboard, but the context is that if the most basic elements are perfected, it completely satisfies the principle of being the best.
I haven't tried all the menus, but I ordered close to 10 menus and they were all the same.
So you can generalize that all menus are like that.

It feels more like a snack than a meal, so from a general perspective, it is suitable as a 'second meal', but
Personally, I think it would be a good idea to visit as a first meal with the intention of ordering a variety of dishes while hungry and experiencing a variety of excellent dishes. If you want to spend some money~

You will find out about the level of customer service when you visit. First of all, there is a sticker board for excellent employees.
I don't know the circumstances of internal employee competition, but in the end, it makes customers happy.

It is a Korean-style Japanese restaurant that has been in operation for the second generation for 40 years since 1986, and a new branch has opened right behind the main building. This place is perfect in terms of taste, atmosphere, and service, and is a place with great experience.
Let's start with green beans and potato chips as a main dish. Let's start the sashimi dinner course with abalone porridge🤗 Kim Soo-sa's soy sauce crab sauce is served, and it's delicious to eat on its own, but it's also perfect dipped in sashimi and sushi.
Assorted sashimi, octopus is so soft, tuna belly, and flounder are all sticky and delicious, starting with flounder sushi, snow crab meat, sweet shrimp, scallops, and tuna sushi. The sushi is the best of all time😘

The stewed cutlassfish has a sweet taste with lotus root and even the texture is a work of art🖌🖌 Anago Tendon shows the essence of fried food👏👏
The nostalgic ttukbaegi roe-bap is also served at Kimsusa, with colorful roe and stir-fried kimchi to suit the tastes of Koreans.

To finish off, the refreshing Kimsusa cod soup commemorating the 40th anniversary of 40 years of boiling and the homemade bean jelly served as dessert were perfect👍

Be sure to visit Kimsusa’s new building, which is fully equipped with table seats, tables, and rooms.

♤ Camoros (12,000₩)

♤ Gomakanpachi (14,000₩)
♤ Shio Yakisoba (18,000₩)
♤ Chicken Karaage (Service)

An izakaya made in Shinsa Mirai. ‘Musasabi’ means flying squirrel in Japanese. It's a more casual place to enjoy than Mirai, and the menu has fewer portions and is cheaper, so it's good to try a variety of things. Personally, I really like Mirai, so I was curious about this place too, and as expected, all the menu items were delicious.

The most recommended menu is Ajiname. It is a dish of horse mackerel seasoned with soybean paste wrapped in seaweed, and the sweet, sour, and savory flavors explode in your mouth. It was surprisingly delicious.

In addition, the Kamoros, which is duck breast seasoned with soy sauce, the Gomakanpachi, which is amberjack seasoned with sesame sauce, and the juicy, garlic-stuffed chicken karaage served as a service, were all impressive, and the Yakisoba that was on the meal menu was also more delicious than most Yakisoba restaurants.

It's a good place to go alone and try a variety of things, or it's a good place to go for 2 or 3 meals with a group.

reviews.author: Zabaroo
reviews.text:
This is an oden specialty restaurant run by a chef who appeared in the Netflix series Black and White Chef. In fact, it was a famous oden restaurant even before it appeared on Black and White Chef, but it seems to have become even more popular after appearing on it. Realistically, if you don't make a reservation, you will have to wait indefinitely, so we recommend making a reservation whenever possible.
The menu sells various types of oden and small dishes that can be eaten as snacks. The alcohol menu sells almost exclusively Japanese alcohol, including beer, highball, sake, and Japanese shochu.
Odeng basically tastes good. The texture and flavor are much better than regular commercial oden. If it's your first time, I recommend trying the assorted oden.
Overall, the soyori dishes are pretty good, so it's a good idea to order more if you don't have enough.
It is a small establishment with about 10 seats and the space between seats is quite tight, so it is not recommended for those who want to have a private conversation.

reviews.author: Chalney
reviews.text:
Odeng Bar, where you can enjoy Japanese-style oden in Korea as well

Food: They sell Japanese-style oden, not Korean-style fish cakes. It is recommended that you research in advance. It was nice that each of the various types of oden was delicious and that you could add whatever sauce you wanted. It was a satisfying meal, although a bit pricey, as it served high-quality Japanese oden, which is difficult to find in Korea. The radish topped with mushroom cream sauce, beef tendon served in a pretty bowl, and chikuwa topped with cheese were especially delicious.

Atmosphere: It felt like a typical Japanese bar with staff in the center and people sitting around them. I liked that they paid attention to the dishes, but it was a bit narrow. It has a dark and noisy atmosphere, so it's good for two people, and it has a unique Japanese bar atmosphere, so you can have a special experience.

Service: Actually, the service was very disappointing. The staff are not only busy, but they don't even look back when I call them and are a bit unfriendly. And when it comes to odeng bars, I wanted them to give me odeng soup as standard, but even after I asked for it, they gave it to me a window later (I think it was more than 10 minutes), which wasn't very pleasant. The bathroom is also located outside on the second floor, which is inconvenient. I was disappointed with the service, perhaps because I had to wait for almost an hour.

This is a review after eating Sang Lokatsu.

I think the elements of Bossam were well incorporated into Los Cutlass.
What does this mean? Is the sirloin part, which can be tough, boiled? The meat felt so moist and soft that you would think, I think it feels like boiled pork. In particular, Sang Lokatsu is composed of sirloin, fat, and neck meat in one piece of tonkatsu, making it feel like pork belly bossam. The sauce actually comes with salted shrimp, and it matches very well. I thought these elements were pretty good.

However, the softness of the batter was a bit disappointing, and the katsu itself was a bit salty, so I recommend eating it with just a little bit of sauce.

reviews.author: ANNEZUE
reviews.text:
I had a lunch meal that was difficult to make a reservation for.
There is no valet, but there is a parking space in front of the store, so you can park right away, and the location is nice and quiet.
The reservation was made for 12 o'clock and the food was served after waiting for about 10 minutes for it to be prepared.
He said there were 8 side dishes and rice, but he suddenly explained the names of the side dishes, such as kelp tamago, tuna akami, jujuro, pickled sancho, anchovies, etc., so I was confused as to where he was starting from. Basically, they explain the location first and what kind of food it is, but this place is inconvenient because you just tell them the ingredients and the customer has to guess which of the eight side dishes it is. They said the side dishes change once every two months, but I don't think I'll come back a second time.

Shigureni made with beef and ginger tasted like sweet beef jerky.

The grilled sea bream aged in yuzu soybean paste had a yuzu scent and the sea bream's flesh felt a bit hard, but overall it was soft and delicious.

The miso soup felt too salty.

The tuna sashimi was salty and sour, and had a soft texture.

The anchovies had a unique taste with a spicy peppery scent. It was an attractive combination that went well together.

The pork cutlet was soggier than I expected, and the sauce had a strong curry flavor. I could taste the curry in the cabbage. It was not tasty. The curry was more of an aroma than a taste, and it felt like a needless way to fill it with side dishes.

The asparagus was crunchy, and the food made with roasted sweet persimmons and turnips and served with nut sauce using pine nuts went well together, had a good texture, was savory, and was delicious. It was the most delicious side dish.

Shomai made with shiitake and shrimp was bland and tasted like bland shrimp balls.

The seasoned dish of spring vegetables and flounder mixed with lemon miso sauce was fragrant and sweet, and went well with the mustard-like sauce.

The kelp tamago egg rolls were moist and soft.

The stick sushi made with cuttlefish and cod roe had a salty and astringent taste, and the rice grains were dry and dry, with a shiso aroma.

Among the side dishes, asparagus, radish, persimmon, spring vegetables, and flounder with lemon miso sauce were the most delicious, but the rest were not so good.

It was disappointing that they kept trying to clear the plate even though the meal wasn't over.

When we finished eating, they gave us ochazuke, which felt like eating oolong tea mixed with hard rice.

Overall, the customer service was not very good, and while they were clearing the table to serve dessert after the meal, they seemed to leave the spilled food intact.

Dorayaki and salt ice cream were served as dessert. The dorayaki contained white bean paste and cheese, and the salt ice cream was salty, sweet, and delicious. The dorayaki had a hard castella-like texture, but it was dry when eaten separately, so it tasted great when eaten together with salt ice cream.

The chef is bright, positive, and personable. When I left after paying, they came to meet me at the entrance of the store and saw me off.

If I had been very satisfied with the lunch, I would have had dinner as well, but since the lunch was unsatisfactory, I don't think I would visit for dinner.
